fact: Maine coons are large cats with thick coats and bushy tails.
Siamese cats often have pale bodies with darker ears, faces, paws, and tails.
Persian cats are known for long fur and round faces.
Ragdolls are large gentle cats with soft coats and blue eyes.
Bengal cats have spotted or marbled coats that can resemble wild cats.
British shorthairs have dense plush coats and round faces.
Sphynx cats have very little fur and need help staying warm.
Scottish folds are known for ears that can fold forward.
Abyssinians are active cats with ticked coats where each hair has bands of color.
American shorthairs are sturdy cats known for many coat colors and patterns.
Norwegian forest cats have thick water-resistant coats suited to cold climates.
Birmans are long-haired cats known for white paws and blue eyes.
Russian blues have short dense coats and bright green eyes.
Oriental shorthairs have long bodies, large ears, and many coat colors.
Devon rex cats have short curly coats and very large ears.
Cornish rex cats have soft wavy coats with almost no guard hairs.
Manx cats are known for naturally short or absent tails.
Turkish angoras are elegant cats with silky coats and long plumed tails.
Turkish vans are strong swimmers and often have color mainly on the head and tail.
Egyptian maus are naturally spotted domestic cats.
Ocicats have wild-looking spots but are fully domestic cats.
Savannah cats are tall, long-legged cats descended from domestic cats and servals.
American curls are named for ears that curl backward.
Selkirk rex cats can have plush curly coats and whiskers.
Himalayans combine long Persian-like coats with pointed coloring.
Balinese cats are long-haired relatives of Siamese cats.
Bombay cats were developed to have sleek black coats and copper-colored eyes.
Burmese cats are muscular, social cats with short glossy coats.
Tonkinese cats combine traits from Siamese and Burmese ancestors.
Chartreux cats are known for blue-gray coats and copper or gold eyes.
Ragamuffins are large affectionate cats with soft plush coats.
Somalis are long-haired relatives of Abyssinians with fluffy tails.
Japanese bobtails have naturally short tails that can look like pom-poms.
American bobtails have naturally shortened tails and sturdy bodies.
LaPerm cats have curly coats that can range from loose waves to tight ringlets.
Singapuras are one of the smallest recognized cat breeds.
Snowshoe cats often have white paws and pointed coloring.
Toygers were bred for striped coats that resemble tiny tigers.
Pixiebobs are sturdy cats often seen with short tails.
Munchkin cats have naturally short legs caused by a genetic trait.
Nebelungs have long blue-gray coats and green eyes.
Siberian cats have thick triple coats suited to cold weather.
Korats are silver-blue cats from Thailand with heart-shaped faces.
Havana browns are known for rich brown coats and green eyes.
European shorthairs are sturdy cats with many traditional coat colors.
Exotic shorthairs have round Persian-like faces but short plush coats.
Chausies are tall athletic cats descended partly from jungle cats.
Lykoi cats have sparse coats that can give them a werewolf-like appearance.
Peterbald cats may be hairless or have very short fine coats.
Burmillas often have silver coats with darker shading at the tips.
Colorpoint shorthairs are closely related to Siamese cats and come in many point colors.

Khao manee cats from Thailand are known for white coats and bright eyes.
Kurilian bobtails have naturally short tails and strong hind legs.
Mekong bobtails are pointed cats with short kinked tails.
Oriental longhairs have slender bodies, large ears, and flowing coats.
Thai cats resemble the traditional rounder form of early Siamese cats.
Tuxedo cats have black-and-white markings that can resemble formal clothing.
Tabby is a coat pattern featuring stripes, spots, or swirls rather than a single breed.
